The web inspector (webinspector.html) is the suite's "browser in the browser" in the reduced form of decision D-004: it loads web pages and shows what they consist of, opens HAR files, and offers a developer-tools bookmarklet for devices where the browser's own developer tools are missing or disabled.

Loading pages needs the for most sites (browsers only allow pages to read other sites that permit it with CORS). HAR files, HTML files, pasted sources and the bookmarklet work without it.

Page

Enter an address and press Load (https:// is added if missing). Choose the user agent (the relay's default, a desktop or a mobile browser) and whether redirects are followed. Open HTML file and Paste source analyse a page without loading it (optionally with its address, so that relative links work).

  • Preview shows the page without scripts, frames and plug-ins; forms do not send. Through the relay, stylesheets, images, background images and fonts are loaded and embedded (up to 80 resources). Click a link to load that page; ← returns to the previous page. The preview size shows the page as on a phone (390 × 844), a tablet (820 × 1180) or a desktop (1366 × 768) instead of the full width; ⟳ turns the device. The page's CSS media queries react to the size.
  • Headers & security lists the response headers and checks HTTPS/HSTS, Content Security Policy (also weakening 'unsafe-inline'/'unsafe-eval'), protection against framing, nosniff, Referrer and Permissions Policy, the cross-origin policies, cookie flags (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite) and version disclosure. ✅ fine, ⚠️ to improve, ❌ missing protection, ℹ️ information.
  • Source shows the HTML with line numbers and highlighting; the search field filters lines; Save source downloads the file.
  • Structure shows title, language, character set, meta tags, the heading outline, links (internal/external), images, scripts, stylesheets, forms and frames, and hints: missing lang, title or viewport, images without alt text, several or no h1, skipped heading levels, form fields without labels, links without text, mixed content.
  • Requests lists every request made for the page and its preview. Save as HAR saves them as a HAR file, Show in HAR viewer opens them in the HAR tab. Block requests takes one rule per line: a host (ads.example.com, also blocks its subdomains) or an address pattern with * (*.woff2, */tracking/*); lines starting with # are comments. The rules apply to the resources of the preview (not to the page itself); Apply and reload loads them again, ⊘ next to a request blocks its host. Blocked requests are crossed out. The rules are remembered in this browser.
  • Cookies lists the cookies the page and its resources set (name, value, domain, path, expiry, Secure/HttpOnly/ SameSite, which request set them); cookies for other sites are rejected as in a browser. With Keep cookies they are stored and sent with later requests that match their domain, path and Secure flag – this way pages behind a login can be inspected after logging in elsewhere in the inspector, or a session cookie can be followed through a site. Stored cookies can be deleted one by one or all at once; they are kept only until the page is closed. Cookies are only visible through the relay (browsers hide Set-Cookie from pages). localStorage and similar storage are filled by scripts, which the preview does not run; the bookmarklet shows them in the real page.

HAR viewer

A HAR file is the network log of a browser (in the developer tools: Network → "Save all as HAR"). Open HAR file (or dropping it onto the window) shows all requests with method, file and host, status (errors in red), type, size, time and a waterfall; the totals show the number of requests, the transferred bytes and the duration. Filter by text or type (document, XHR/JSON, JS, CSS, images, fonts, media, other); click a column heading to sort.

Click a request for details: Headers (general, response and request headers), Query (parameters and request body), Body (the response; JSON pretty-printed, images shown), Cookies and Timing (blocked, DNS, connect, TLS, send, wait, receive). Copy as cURL copies the request as a curl command.

Bookmarklet

The bookmarklet opens a small developer-tools panel at the bottom of any page:

  • Console: console.* output and errors since the panel was opened, and an input line that runs JavaScript in the page.
  • Elements: Pick element, then click an element of the page: CSS path, size and position, attributes, computed styles and HTML; Parent goes up.
  • Network: the resources the page loaded (from the Resource Timing API) with size and time.
  • Storage: cookies, localStorage and sessionStorage.
  • Info: address, title, user agent, viewport, language and meta tags.

Install it by dragging the 🔍 Inspector link to the bookmarks bar. On phones: Copy code, create a bookmark of any page, edit it and replace its address with the copied code; then open the page to inspect and choose the bookmark (in Chrome for Android, type the bookmark's name into the address bar and tap the suggestion). Choosing it again hides the panel. Try it on this page opens it in the inspector itself.

Pages whose Content Security Policy forbids eval() still show the panel, but the console input cannot run code there.

Limits

The preview is not a full browser: no scripts (pages that are built by JavaScript stay empty or incomplete), no logins (unless cookies are kept), no forms. Pages behind a login can be analysed by saving them in the browser and opening the HTML file, or by recording a HAR file.

Keyboard shortcuts

On a Mac, use Cmd instead of Ctrl. F1 (or ?) shows this list in the application.
